assessment.completionStatus: Successful — all six acceptance criteria (AC1–AC6) verified end-to-end against the local MockSite and the source-built backend. AC3 needed a retry because of one intermittent 0-byte capture episode; every other step worked on the first attempt.
assessment.successRate: 93% — 6/6 criteria passed; 3 of 4 AC3 crawl attempts were clean, one lost 4/6 pages to the reliability bug; no step failed for documentation or discoverability reasons.
assessment.majorBlockers: None permanent. Two friction points slowed the run: (1) the intermittent 0-byte capture failure in the first depth>=1 crawl forced an investigation and a re-run; (2) MockSite's cold Maven preflight served nothing on :18080 for ~17 minutes (documented as 10–15 min), which looks like a stall to a first-time user. The stale-bundle state resolved itself automatically via the first browser command.
assessment.mostConfusingAspects: The stale-bundle startup messaging: help/status announced a manual rebuild and 'dev mode refuses to start', yet the next normal command rebuilt and started by itself — the three messages describe different behaviours for the same state, and status mixed in an unrelated globally installed bundle version. Also confusing: a crawl whose pages all failed to deliver content is reported by `crawl result` as backend status 'OK' while only `crawl list` shows 'partial failure (2 of 6 pages ok)' (documented trade-off, so not filed as an issue).
assessment.mostValuableImprovements: 1) Fix the intermittent capture failure (0-byte contentLength with HTTP 200) so crawl never records an empty page as delivered — it is the only defect that silently loses data. 2) Unify the stale-bundle messages and make it explicit that the next browser command rebuilds automatically. 3) Align per-command `--help` texts with the reference docs (loop state path, swarm auto-prune) — the references are accurate, the help strings lag. 4) Consider a startup banner/line for the MockSite preflight so the 10–15-minute build is visibly 'working', not 'hung'.

issues.title: Intermittent 0-byte page captures in crawl link-discovery mode (browser runtime injection failure)

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 crawl "http://localhost:18080/generated/crawl/index.html" -d 2 -ol "a.product" -olp "product/"
(Observed on the first run after backend startup, against MockSite fixture pages that had stale ~75h-old page-store entries. 4 of 6 discovered pages came back empty.)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: All discovered pages on an already-running local site fetch with content; no pages reported as '0 bytes'.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: 4 of 6 pages were recorded with httpStatus 200 but contentLength 0 and no title; CLI printed '⚠ 4 of 6 page(s) had fetch or extraction errors' and exited non-zero (documented exit 6); 'crawl list' recorded 'partial failure (2 of 6 pages ok)'. Backend log: 'WARN ... JavaScript is not injected | .../product/2.html' and 'WARN ... The Browser4 runtime (__pulsar_utils__) is not available on this page (re-injection failed); capture continues without the runtime-dependent helpers'; the failed loads took up to 10.011s (= MAX_JAVASCRIPT_INJECTION_RETRIES 10 x JAVASCRIPT_INJECTION_POLL_MS 1000ms). An immediate re-run (--refresh) fetched 10/10 pages; a later run without --refresh and a run after a cold backend restart also fetched 10/10 — the failure is intermittent, not deterministic. No in-run retry appears in the backend log for the failed URLs.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Inferred: on some page loads (observed in a depth>=1 crawl that reuses shared tab-pool tabs), the driver-side runtime script (__pulsar_utils__) never became available; waitForJavascriptInjected polls 10x1s and times out, and the bounded re-injection in ensurePulsarUtils also fails. Capture then 'continues without the runtime-dependent helpers' and produced a zero-length document while the protocol status stayed 200. The crawl records it as a found-but-empty page rather than a delivery failure, and the depth>=1 delivery retry (resolveDeliveryAttempt) did not re-load the URL within the run. Why injection fails intermittently needs backend investigation — a likely candidate is a tab/driver binding race on reused tabs, consistent with the existing 'protocol-handler deregistration races' comment that motivated the shared-session design for depth-0 seeds (CrawlRoundRunner.crawlDepth0).
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-protocol/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/protocol/browser/emulator/impl/InteractiveBrowserEmulator.kt:waitForJavascriptInjected() and ensurePulsarUtils(); retry decision: browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/api/service/crawl/CrawlRoundRunner.kt:resolveDeliveryAttempt() (CrawlSupport.kt:577)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Treat contentLength==0 as a delivery failure in the depth>=1 path and force the one retry (resolveDeliveryAttempt) even when a parse event fired with a non-empty document, so a zero-byte capture cannot settle a URL as success.
- Log the injection timeout at WARN with task id + tab/session id in the crawl context, so the race that causes 'JavaScript is not injected' is diagnosable from logs.
- For a page whose runtime is missing, prefer re-navigating on a freshly created tab over continuing capture without the runtime helpers, and consider a longer/backoff injection window.
- Add an e2e assertion that every discovered page in a MockSite fixture crawl has contentLength > 0 and a non-empty title.

issues.title: Stale-bundle diagnostics mislead: wrapper demands a manual rebuild and status claims 'dev mode refuses to start', while browser commands auto-rebuild and start

sections.body:
On a checkout whose sources look newer than the built bundle:
1. ./b4w.ps1 help  -> 'Backend sources changed since the runtime bundle was last built. Rebuild with: $env:BROWSER4_CLI_FORCE_REBUILD_BUNDLE = "1"; b4w <command>'
2. ./b4w.ps1 status -> 'Matches checkout: no (sources_newer_than_bundle) — dev mode refuses to start'
3. ./b4w.ps1 goto about:blank -> auto-rebuilds the bundle (~5.5 min) and starts the backend, with no manual flag
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: One consistent story: either the stale-bundle state automatically resolves on the next browser command (message should say so), or it genuinely refuses to start (and then it should refuse).
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Three different messages; the status text explicitly says the mode refuses to start, yet the very next browser command rebuilds and starts unattended. The same status output also prints 'Installed bundle: v4.14.0' and '⚠ Version mismatch: CLI is 4.14.1 but installed backend is v4.14.0', which refers to a globally installed bundle that dev mode does not run — noise that can send a first-time user chasing the wrong problem. The warning also prints for purely local commands that never touch the backend (help, config).
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The staleness check distinguishes two kinds (version_mismatch vs sources_newer_than_bundle), but daemon.rs:report_rows() renders the hard-refusal wording ('dev mode refuses to start') for both, while the launcher treats sources_newer_than_bundle as 'rebuild then start'. Separately, b4w.ps1 prints the manual-rebuild notice for every invocation while the mismatch persists, even though the CLI would rebuild automatically on demand; the installed-bundle version line is compared without excluding dev-mode runs.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/daemon.rs:7391 (LocalBundleProvenance::report_rows) and b4w.ps1:455 (backend-source hash check)
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Render per-kind status text: 'sources newer than bundle — the next browser command rebuilds and starts it automatically' vs the true refusal wording only for version_mismatch.
- Gate the b4w.ps1 rebuild notice to commands that will actually use the backend, or drop it in favour of a one-line note that the rebuild is automatic.
- When the dev-mode local bundle is present, suppress or clearly label the 'Installed bundle' version-mismatch line as unrelated to dev mode.
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

review.notes: FIXED 2026-10-24 (working tree, branch feat/agent-run-interactive) — 3/3 sub-items addressed. (1) report_rows() now renders the per-kind action through mismatch_action(): sources_newer_than_bundle reads 'the next browser command rebuilds and starts it automatically', and only version_mismatch keeps 'dev mode refuses to start' (test: report_rows_name_the_action_dev_mode_actually_takes). (2) b4w.ps1 no longer demands a manual rebuild: one line says the next backend command rebuilds automatically, printed only for commands that can start the backend (Test-B4wMayStartBackend, mirroring should_ensure_server_running()) and suppressed under -Rebuild; the backend content hash now covers src/main of the bundled modules only and drops browser4-plugins (its jars ship in plugins/, not lib/), so plugin-only or test-only edits no longer announce a rebuild. (3) The dev-mode 'Installed bundle' line was already labelled '— used only outside a repository checkout' and the CLI-vs-installed-bundle warning is gated behind !dev_mode, so no further change was needed (verified with the backend both down and up). Verification: cargo test --bin browser4-cli detect_staleness 10 passed; pwsh bin/tests/b4w.tests.ps1 129/129 passed; live probes — plugin-only and test-only edits keep 'Matches checkout: yes' with no notice, a browser4-agent-tools/src/main edit flips it to stale with the notice.

issues.title: swarm create --help does not mention that prior sessions' completed swarm tasks are pruned automatically

sections.body:
./b4w.ps1 swarm create --max-browser-contexts 2 --max-open-tabs 4
-> 'Auto-cleaned 12 completed swarm task(s) from prior sessions (non-interactive auto-clean; use `swarm list` before `swarm create` if you need to keep them): <12 ids>'

sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The command help should disclose the automatic pruning (and the absence of an opt-out), as the swarm.md reference does.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: A user reading only --help learns of --clear-stale but not that every swarm create silently prunes the tracked completed tasks of prior sessions (there is no --keep flag). The tracked task list of a previous session is gone unless `swarm list` was captured first; results themselves are retained, and the runtime message does name the pruned ids.
